item.subject: science
item.stem:
Meena connects a copper wire to a cell in her classroom in Jaipur. She holds a magnetic compass close to the wire and then presses the switch so that current flows through the wire.
What should happen to the compass needle, and why?

options.A: The needle deflects, because the current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it.
options.B: The needle does not move, because a compass needle moves only near a permanent magnet.
options.C: The needle deflects only after the wire becomes hot from the current.
options.D: The needle does not move, because copper is not a magnetic material.
